answer: Submissions that land within 153 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The dune detector writes to lagoon, and vertex reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 11 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 8 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
